what_it_does: When chip designers want to check how fast signals travel through a circuit before the wires are physically drawn (called pre-routing timing prediction), they typically ignore how the power delivery network — the grid of wires that supplies electricity across the chip — affects signal delays. Voltage fluctuations in that power grid (called IR drop, because voltage loss equals current times resistance) and crowded wire regions where signals compete for routing space both distort timing, but existing machine learning prediction tools leave those effects out. This paper adds two specialized feature extractors — one that encodes the IR drop pattern, another that encodes routing congestion — and combines them with the circuit's logical description through an optimization strategy that balances how much each source contributes to the final timing prediction. The approach is validated on real 16-nanometer chip designs from TSMC.
